candidates.title: SelfBench repository agent benchmarks

ease.reason: A one-repository prototype can follow the documented web workflow, though it needs GitHub, agents, and sandbox setup.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: engineering teams may pay for repository-specific comparisons; the sources show no validated demand or revenue.

feasibility.reason: A manually bounded demo is conceivable, but task validation, agent runs, and a safe sandbox are substantial two-week work.

autonomy.reason: Batch generation continues after closing the page, while people approve tasks and select runs.

evidence.reason: First-party documentation describes the app workflow and public leaderboards, without verified independent use or outcomes.

candidates.reason: Fresh checker feedback caps feasibility at 5 and evidence at 6; with the other supported ratings the unrounded mean is 5.6, below the threshold of 6.

rejected.title: SelfBench repository agent benchmarks
rejected.reason: The repair-adjusted ratings are ease 6, profit 5, feasibility 5, autonomy 6, and evidence 6: mean 5.6, below threshold 6. The first-party docs establish a product workflow but not independent customer use; a safe sandbox and task validation make a beginner two-week build too substantial for a qualifying feasibility score.

steps.message: Reassessed the sole repair candidate against the fresh checker feedback. Its supported feasibility and evidence ceilings produce a mean below policy threshold, so no post is proposed.
